question: Does the neural-rate gW advantage replicate when a finite reversible buffer stores a mediator and releases it after shutoff?
kinetics: For each source and each of its three channels, z is the free mediator, b is bound, and h is the downstream filter. Flux J=kon*z*(B-b)-koff*b. dz/dt=k*(a-z)-J, db/dt=J, dh/dt=k*(z-h). The target retains the previous direct and delayed signed readouts. Independent of the original occupancy-gated speed law. Capacity B in [0.45,1.0], kon in [2.5,5.5], koff in [0.22,0.6] sampled per source/channel independently of wiring. At constant activity z=h=a. Neither bound mediator nor kinetic constants are observed by the models. Constant control uses previous constant generator on the very same new graphs.
holdouts: Inherit all train/validation/test pulses, sampling indices, observed control covariance, five-time distance and metrics from hashed reference. New evaluation innovations shared across regimes, budgets and models; fresh topology/parameter/noise seeds. Test the whole directly simulated 4:1 swap.
budgets: Both budgets trained from scratch on byte-identical data, same two initializations and minibatch prefix per network/regime. Each budget uses its own complete cosine decay. 2400 is primary; same-data 600 comparison is descriptive. Freeze both weights and forecasts before either budget sees a test outcome.
decision: Same as pilot: two-sided 95% network-level paired t intervals Bonferroni-adjusted across six contrasts (two regimes by three primary endpoints). Neural vs two-rate requires upper log-MSE ratio confidence limits below 1 on ratio scale (full and five-time tail), and lower recovery difference limit above -1 percentage point in buffered regime. Dense tail, pulse family comparisons and 600-step results descriptive. More recovery is claimed only when the primary lower limit exceeds 0.
audit: Validate buffered dynamics with independent total-mediator formulation and DOP853, check mass balance, steady state and zero-capacity limit, split disjointness, frozen hashes and test metrics. Report late checkpoint frequency. No hyperparameter or simulator parameter selection on test outcomes.
